<!-- pr-reviewer: 0e1839fac2974d1314111848cded155b054816f5 -->
**Needs changes before merge** (one safety item, one small one). Thanks @JSwetz - the wiring is tidy and well tested.

**What looks good**
- Math checks out: `offset = -dot(origin, axis)` puts the CIP origin at Z=0 with +Z toward the spindle; the fixture (CIP origin (0,0,-75)) gives 75 mm and the profile test pins foot 35 / top 75.
- Refusal is by name for no coordinate systems, degenerate ones and unreadable files; the editor falls back to the manual numeric placement with a note, and the pick-tip/pick-axis paths still work (they now set a "manual placement" note).
- `SetToolBody::from_step_auto` goes through `SetToolBody::new`, so it is validated at creation and undoable like the existing path. No new `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, no new dependency, no build.rs/scripts/.github change, no snapshot PNG changes, no CHANGELOG.md edit, `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #370` present, clean-room sources only (ISO 13399 naming).

**Local results (trial-merged with current upstream/main; merge was clean)**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_csys` | 9 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tool_body` | 12 passed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib tool_body` (CWD crates/ui) | 10 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
1. `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs` (`align_tool_body`, ~lines 209-228): the CSIF fallback can silently mis-place the tool. CSIF is the interface coordinate system (where the tool meets the holder), not the cutting point, so its origin as the "tip" puts the body wrong - the same reasoning the decision file uses to drop PCS/MCS. Also, if CIP exists but is ambiguous or was refused as degenerate, the code falls through to CSIF instead of refusing. Please use CIP only (refuse by name when it is missing, ambiguous or degenerate), or, if you have a published ISO 13399 reference that makes CSIF the cutting reference for some item class, cite it in the code and decision file and never fall back from a refused CIP. Add a test for "CIP degenerate + CSIF valid must refuse".
2. `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_body_page.rs` (~line 86) / `state_tool_body.rs`: the note "aligned by ISO 13399 coordinate systems" stays on screen after the user edits the axis combo or offset field by hand (only the pick paths reset it to "manual placement"), so the label can claim an alignment that no longer holds. Clear it on those edits.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- Units: are the mesh from `load_model` and the CSYS origin from `read_tool_csys` in the same unit for an inch STEP file? A test with a non-mm fixture, or a note that both are already normalised, would settle it.
- `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_csys.rs` is now 403 lines (flag only, ~400 guideline).
- `Fixes #370` will close the umbrella issue; if more slices of #370 remain, `Refs #370` may be intended.
- Snapshot suites were not touched or run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
